transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Redwood Legal Ops), Liam O'Neill (Asterion Procurement), Sara Morales (Asterion CISO), Devon Park (Asterion Platform), Nadia Kim (Asterion Legal), Omar Ruiz (Asterion FinOps)

Summary (auto):
Asterion is evaluating Redwood for API-hosted inference with a path to private deployment. Primary asks: strict data residency and KMS integration, SLA/uptime and rollback policy, pricing clarity for mixed hosted + reserved capacity model, and legal redlines on DPA/MSA. Next steps agreed around pricing worksheet, network diagram, and DPA redlines.

Topics:
- MSA and DPA redline expectations
- SLA tiers (99.9 vs 99.95) and service credits
- Dedicated vs Hosted run-rate and burst model
- KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys
- Data residency and audit logging

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um we should probably start with quick intros and then dive into each of the three asks we got from Nadia last week.
[00:12] Liam O'Neill: Thanks Jordan. I'm Liam, procurement. Quick context: we're running a vendor gate on July 15th so this call's to unblock legal and security questions, and cost assumptions that feed FinOps.
[00:22] Sara Morales: Sara, CISO. Main items: encryption at rest keys, SSO, audit logs, and data residency. We'll need to see SOC2 report and encryption flow.
[00:31] Devon Park: Devon, platform eng. We'll own the integration and run the perf tests. The main technical constraint is p95 latency under 400ms for short responses and the ability to pin a model version.
[00:43] Jordan Patel: Great. At a high level Redwood supports hosted API with per-token billing, dedicated reserved pools, and an on-prem/private deployment option. For customers with strict residency we do private control plane or VPC peering.
[00:58] Maya Chen: To add, our runtime supports KV cache and automatic prefix caching which helps cost and latency, but for private setups we do an extra handshake for the KMS flow.
[01:10] Sara Morales: When you say KMS flow, is that customer-managed key inside our HSM, or you manage the keys? We need customer-managed KMS so keys never leave our control.
[01:20] Priya Rao: We can integrate with customer KMS. Typically we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM via a key-wrap model. In private deployments we can do key material stay-on-customer side with enveloping.
[01:34] Nadia Kim: For contract redlines, we usually ask for explicit language that data will not be used for model training and that audit logs are available for 13 months. Where does Redwood sit on that?
[01:46] Alex Gomez: On the MSA/DPA point, our standard is no training on customer data and we include audit logs. The DPA already states 12 months by default but we can discuss 13 months as an SLA add-on. Need to route that through legal.
[02:01] Omar Ruiz: From FinOps side, we need a pricing model that'll mix hosted low-volume calls with reserved capacity for spikes. Can you share an example TCO?
[02:12] Jordan Patel: Yes, we'll send a pricing worksheet. Quick preview — typical pattern is baseline reserved capacity in Redwood Dedicated to cover steady throughput, plus hosted for unpredictable burst. Pricing differs significantly at scale; reserved units drop per-inference cost by ~30-45% depending on model.
[02:30] Devon Park: Any hard guarantees on latency for dedicated pools vs hosted? We can't afford consistent tail latencies.
[02:36] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives stronger isolation and we can hit tighter SLOs — for the models you're looking at we can practically get p95 ~120-180ms depending on seq length. Hosted may vary more, especially at peak. Also we have regional routing, so if you choose EU region, that'll help residency and latency.
[02:56] Liam O'Neill: About SLAs — can you do 99.95% for production endpoints? Our procurement prefers 99.95 with service credits scaling. If you require a higher price for that that's fine but we need clarity.
[03:10] Jordan Patel: 99.95 is available on Dedicated with SLA add-on. For hosted standard tier we typically offer 99.9. The difference is around redundancy and reserved capacity commitments. We'll put the tiers in the worksheet.
[03:22] Sara Morales: Also, we need SSO via SAML and RBAC so different teams have different access. Can Redwood integrate with our enterprise SSO and SCIM?
[03:31] Maya Chen: Yes — we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For private deployments that's customer controlled. We also emit detailed audit logs at the token and request level, but note logs can be redacted; we'll show examples.
[03:46] Nadia Kim: For the DPA redlines I'm seeing some standard language around subprocessors. We need a list of subprocessors and is there subcontractor-level encryption?
[03:55] Alex Gomez: We'll supply a subprocessors list. For encryption our transit is TLS1.2+ and at-rest uses AES-256. For private deployments the customer's KMS/HSM controls the root.
[04:07] Devon Park: On the integration side, we plan to run a 2-week pilot with a controlled traffic shape. We'd like to run dedicated capacity for the pilot to validate latency and cost. Any minimums?
[04:20] Jordan Patel: For pilot dedicated we'll do a limited reserved pool — usually a 1-month minimum for reserved pools but we can be flexible for pilots, e.g., 30-day reserved with prorated billing. We'll include pilot pricing scenarios.
[04:35] Liam O'Neill: Egress — curious how you measure network egress and if there are extra fees for cross-region traffic, particularly for EU/UK data.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Egress fees depend on deployment. Hosted often includes egress to your configured region, cross-region egress is billable. For Private we can peer and you pay your cloud egress costs; we can document expected numbers for common workloads.
[04:59] Sara Morales: We also want to know about breach notification timelines and access to forensic logs. That's a must for our security review.
[05:09] Alex Gomez: Standard breach notification is 72 hours. We can include more specific for contractual high-priority incidents. For forensic logs, we provide structured logs and can support a runbook.
[05:22] Devon Park: LP — small nit, sometimes transcripts call KV cache 'KV cash', just a heads up for searches.
[05:28] Jordan Patel: (laughs) noted.
[05:31] Nadia Kim: On DPA — do you support data residency carve-outs for EU-only processing, i.e., all tokens and logs stay in EU region?
[05:40] Priya Rao: Yes. We can do region lock for processing and storage. For audit logs retention in EU we can put the storage bucket in EU and route logs there. We'll share the network diagram and config options.
[05:52] Omar Ruiz: About cost — what's the unit for embeddings and generation? Embeddings per-embedding call, and generation per token? We need a mapping to our current volume.
[06:03] Jordan Patel: Correct. Embeddings are billed per call with vector size assumptions; generation billed per input+output token. We'll include sample conversions in the worksheet so you can model projected spend.
[06:13] Liam O'Neill: Competitors question — we've been reviewing Anthropic and Bedrock; can you call out major differentiation on contracts and security?
[06:21] Jordan Patel: Contractually we focus on production-grade SLAs, a runbook for fallback, and private deployment options with customer-managed KMS. Some competitors offer hosted-only or limited private modes. We'll summarize in the deck.
[06:34] Sara Morales: One more security ask: can Redwood support a SOC2 audit with customer-specific scope or at least produce SSAE evidence?
[06:42] Alex Gomez: We can provide the SOC2 Type II report and a SOC2 summary; customer-specific attestation is more complex but we can provide supporting evidence and collaborate on SOC questionnaires.
[06:54] Jordan Patel: Ok, to make sure we close the loop, recap the deliverables: pricing worksheet and TCO scenarios, private deployment network diagram & KMS notes, subprocessors list and SOC2 artifacts, and draft DPA redline language.
[07:06] Nadia Kim: Correct — we'll aim to return redlines by July 6th.
[07:12] Jordan Patel: Great. Any other questions?
[07:15] Devon Park: One quick technical — does Redwood provide KV cache warmup APIs so we can pre-warm for predictable low-latency responses?
[07:24] Maya Chen: We have a pre-warm library and APIs for priming KV caches and pinning tokens. We'll share the docs link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kv-cache-warmup and a short runbook.
[07:37] Omar Ruiz: Also need line items for egress & data residency premium in the worksheet so finance can pre-approve.
[07:44] Jordan Patel: Understood — we'll call out egress assumptions and a separate line for residency premium.
[07:50] Liam O'Neill: Ok that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[07:52] Jordan Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and the worksheet.
